newsitem.title: JAPAN: Foley to be new U.S. ambassador to Japan-report.
newsitem.headline: Foley to be new U.S. ambassador to Japan-report.

text.p: Former U.S. House Speaker Thomas Foley is expected to be appointed the new ambassador to Japan, Japanese media reported on Friday.

Japan's Kyodo news agency, quoting U.S. administration sources, said U.S. President Bill Clinton has selected the 68-year-old former House Speaker to take up the post, which has been vacant since December.
Clinton is expected to make a formal announcement next week, Kyodo said.
A spokeswoman at the U.S. embassy in Tokyo said she was not aware of any announcement on a new ambassador in the immediate future.

Foley was a House member from Washington State for 30 years from 1965 until he lost his reelection bid in December 1994. He served as House Speaker, the highest post in the House of Representatives, from 1989 to 1994.

The previous ambassador, former U.S. vice president Walter Mondale, retired in December after a three-year tenure during which he played a key role in settling trade feuds and repairing frayed security ties.
Foley was a moderately liberal member of Congress, not particularly active in trade issues.
He is expected to bring to the job a close knowledge of the inner workings of Washington rather than a deep knowledge of Japan.

When George Bush was president, Foley led the opposition to U.S. involvement in the Gulf War. He takes the liberal stand against the death penalty and favours a woman's right to abortion, both contentious issues in America.
Among his other roles, he was chairman of the House Agriculture Committee from 1975 to 1981.
